title: Tippecanoe Place: the Studebaker Mansion in South Bend, and the Voices People Report

beats.text: Voices. Pictures, swinging on the walls. That's what people have reported inside Tippecanoe Place, in South Bend.
beats.label: SOUTH BEND, INDIANA
beats.credit: What people report: ABC57 (2019); visitor accounts

beats.text: Wagon maker Clem Studebaker had this 40-room stone mansion built. It was finished in 1889.
beats.label: THE STUDEBAKER MANSION
beats.credit: History: National Park Service; SAH Archipedia

beats.text: That same year, fire tore through it. The roof burned. Much of the inside was gutted. But the stone walls survived.
beats.label: FIRE
beats.credit: National Park Service; Univ. of Notre Dame; South Bend News-Times

beats.text: It was restored within a year. Clem died in 1901. In World War 2, the house was a Red Cross headquarters. Later, it was a school for disabled children.
beats.label: AFTER THE STUDEBAKERS
beats.credit: National Park Service; SAH Archipedia; Wikipedia

beats.text: Legend says some of the Studebakers never left.
beats.label: THE LEGEND

beats.text: The restaurant closed in January 2026. Please view it from the road.
beats.label: TODAY

beats.text: Comment your town, and it could be next.

end_card.pill: South Bend, Indiana: view it from the road

factcheck.result: Line 1 'have reported' (closed now); line 3 'much of the inside'; line 4 restored within a year, school came after WWII; line 5 trimmed; mansion redrawn with a square tower and a small round turret, no interiors; adult shadow figure; all supported
